newsitem.title: INDIA: India court rejects "Bandit Queen's" plea.
newsitem.headline: India court rejects "Bandit Queen's" plea.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Friday rejected former "Bandit Queen" Phoolan Devi's plea for protection against arrest, paving the way for her trial in 57 legal cases including murder, court officials said.
A two-judge bench dismissed the member of parliament's request for anticipatory, or pre-emptive, bail in the cases.

But the Supreme Court said that later this month it would take up Devi's appeal against a ruling by the Uttar Pradesh state high court which had dismissed the state government's request to have all pending criminal cases against quashed.
Devi, who belongs to the low-caste Mallah community of boatmen, shot to notoriety after 22 upper-caste men were killed in a massacre at Behmai village in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh in 1981.
She was accused of leading a gang in the massacre but she denied the charges. Devi surrendered to the police in 1983 under a special amnesty offered by the central state of Madhya Pradesh.
Devi spent more than 10 years in prison before being released in 1994.
Movie maker Sekhar Kapoor portrayed Devi as a low-caste heroine in the biographical film "Bandit Queen" which won praise at international film festivals.
Devi, who is illiterate, was elected to parliament as a member of the Samajwadi Party, a socialist party of low-caste Hindus, in general elections last year.
The Supreme Court said that it would not grant Devi pre-emptive bail or parole, and that the trial in all 57 cases should proceed.

But it said she could seek anticipatory bail from a lower court. It also agreed to hold a hearing on January 31 on her appeal against the state ruling as well as her request to have the criminal trial shifted out of Uttar Pradesh state.
